parsed.answer: Pyridostatin (PDS) is explicitly described as a G4-stabilizing compound in the retrieved evidence, and telomeres are listed among G4-forming genomic sequences. This is corroborated by the telomeric phenotype: PDS increased telomere fragility in BRCA2-deficient cells, consistent with stabilized telomeric G-quadruplexes driving telomere instability. The claim is therefore directly supported by the corpus excerpts, which characterize PDS as a G4-stabilizer acting on telomeric G4 structures.
